comments.body: 2026-11-05, another instance under the installed release: Codex worker galaxy (0.166.0) got a wake for galaxy+ocean #13 after it had read #13 and #14 and posted #15; the prescribed read said nothing unread. No resume involved this time. Consistent with a codex queue wake stored before the read and taken after it, which the typed-only delivery being built today removes.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: Done 2026-11-05 (9d218f4f, 276936d9): reproduced a codex queue wake stored after its message was read and replayed on resume; codex queue has no cancel, so Muster no longer stores wakes there. Copies an older Muster already stored can still replay once.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Codex helpers receive wake prompts claiming messages are still unread after their first successful read. Each stale wake starts another turn, and the requested read prints `nothing unread`.

Seen 2026-10-27 in the authorized Muster round, after repeatedly resuming the same conversations to recover from a Codex code-mode host failure. Opal read #4-10 in opal+voyage and posted #11, then received stale `still unread` wakes for #4-8 and #4-9. Both subsequent `muster msg read --group opal+voyage` calls returned exit 0 and `nothing unread`. Jade saw the same pattern for #4-9 after its successful read.

No message body was lost. It is unclear whether these were delayed terminal input, queued Codex steering prompts, or stale daemon wake state. The worker session IDs are 01a17fc5-c172-7bf2-b4dc-e9566acbc604 and 01a17fc5-c1af-7c21-a7c7-8917304882a2. Round evidence is under /tmp/muster-round-20261027.6S6lF0; opal+voyage #12 records the report. Preserve the distinction from the Claude Code Stop/PostToolUse duplicate-delivery card a_2pOTJDMPl.
title: Muster: resumed Codex gets wakes for already-read messages
